title: Signal throttling & cognitive-overload mitigation — sketches and heuristics (WIP)
content:
Summary:
Quick exploration of UX patterns for reducing alert noise and cognitive overload in the Console. Focus: throttling, digesting, and prioritization heuristics that sit between metric SLOs and notification fanout. Goal is to give oncall/owners predictable, controllable signal while preserving fast time-to-detect for real regressions.

Context and motivation:
- Feedback from SRE and customer trials: too many low-signal alerts during traffic spikes (batch jobs, rollout churn). People start muting channels or ignoring alerts.
- Existing console has threshold-based alerts + routing; need intermediate layer for "signal shaping" before fanout.
- Want defaults that are safe for small teams but adjustable for enterprises (auditability + rollback).

Core ideas (high level):
1) Signal buckets: classify incoming triggers into buckets (Immediate, Near-term digest, Adaptive-suppressed, Ignored-with-telemetry). Buckets are computed by heuristics and user rules.
2) Decay & suppression functions: if a signal repeats within X seconds/minutes and doesn't exceed severity delta, throttle to digest. Decay schedule should be configurable per-route/model.
3) Priority-weighted digest: group related events into a single digest with headline + top-3 details; include counts and top traces. Allow manual "expand" for full list.
4) Adaptive thresholds: baseline thresholds adapt based on rolling baseline (p95 baseline over last 24h) + seasonality (time-of-day). Conservative by default, opt-in ML-based adjustments later.
5) Escalation windows & escalation amplification: if a suppressed signal keeps recurring and severity increases, automatically escalate to Immediate.

Wireframe notes (UI components):
- Route-level "Signal Settings" panel (right rail) with:
  - Mode (Enforce | Observe-only | Simulation)
  - Suppression profile dropdown (Default / Aggressive / Minimal / Custom)
  - Decay window slider (30s, 1m, 5m, 15m, custom)
  - Grouping heuristics toggles (by error class, by trace root cause, by host/pod)
  - Preview: simulated 1-hour feed showing how many notifications would be suppressed/digested

- Global "Noise Dashboard" (top-level):
  - Incoming signals per minute + suppressed rate (%)
  - Top 5 suppressed routes and why (pattern match: flapping, high-cardinality, transient latency)
  - Cost estimate: tokens/time saved by digesting vs immediate fanout

- Digest view (notification inbox style):
  - Timeline with collapsible groups: header shows summary (n events, severity spread, first/last timestamp)
  - CTA: Mark as acknowledged / Route to incident / Open playbook / Re-run detection on expanded set

Example flow (oncall):
1) Spike in 503s on /generate, baseline triple but typical for batch job -> Signal Settings detects repetition -> routes to digest every 5m
2) Digest sent to oncall Slack at 5m with counts + top trace; if subsequent 503s continue and error rate crosses secondary threshold, an immediate alert fires and escalates to oncall pagers

Heuristic sketches (pseudocode-style, intentionally high level):
- repeat_suppression_rule(route, window, severity_delta):
  - if events_of_type(route, window) > N and max_severity - min_severity < severity_delta -> mark as digest
- adaptive_baseline(route):
  - baseline = weight(past_24h_p95, past_7d_p95_time_of_day)
  - threshold = baseline * multiplier(profile)

Open UX questions (need product/eng tradeoffs):
- Preview accuracy: how expensive to run simulation in realtime for each change? Can we use a sampled window?
- Who should own suppression policies at org scale? route owner, team, or global SRE?
- Audit trail: must be clear in incident history which alerts were suppressed vs duplicated — legal/compliance concern for private deployments.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Route-level suppression toggle with 3 preset profiles + custom slider
- Digest grouping by error class + counts; one digest delivered per grouping window to configured destination (Slack/email)
- Simulation preview showing suppressed vs immediate events for last 60 minutes (sampled)
- Instrumentation: metrics for suppressed_count, digest_count, false_negative_incidents (cases where suppression missed a real regression)

Edge cases and gotchas:
- High-cardinality noise (e.g., per-user errors) requires grouping keys or cardinality heuristics; otherwise digest headers are meaningless. Consider auto-detection of high-cardinality signals and recommend aggregation keys.
- Feedback loop: if users repeatedly expand a digest and act on one item, surface that as a signal to promote that pattern to immediate in future (learning).
- Multi-route correlated incidents: suppression must be aware of correlation (same upstream service) or risk hiding a systemic failure. Need cross-route correlation detector.

Small policy composer UX notes (rough):
- Drag-and-drop conditions: metric, time-window, cardinality, spike-delta, noise-profile
- Live test button: run rule against sampled history -> show sample event groups
- Quick presets for "quiet hours" and "maintenance windows" with optional auto-unmute

Telemetry and metrics to display in Console (dashboard suggestions):
- Suppressed rate (global and by route)
- Time-to-first-notify for incidents that were suppressed vs not suppressed
- Alert fatigue index: a composite of suppression rate, ack latency, and alerts-per-oncall-per-week
- Digest usefulness signal: fraction of digests that were expanded / escalated / led to an incident

Operational considerations for Dedicated/Private:
- All suppression decisions must be reversible and logged to customer audit logs. Provide an exportable suppression-audit CSV for compliance teams.
- Default conservative policy for private installs; allow admins to opt-in to aggressive suppression.

Design TODOs / next steps:
- Work with eng (Omar) to prototype a simulation backend (sample-based) to drive preview widget.
- Create 3-4 Figma frames for rail + digest inbox + global noise dashboard (Lena).
- Product: define policy presets and default multipliers; run customer interviews with 3 pilot SRE teams.
- SRE: sketch correlation detector: simple heuristics first (shared upstream host, identical error traces).

Notes to self / fragments:
- "digest headline should show most-likely-root-cause tag" (from convo w/eng)
- Consider "quiet-hours stenographic mode" where low-severity digests are only emailed once/day but still visible in console
- Link to pagerduty/opsgenie: preserve event IDs so that if digest escalates it's easy to trace back to original events

References / links (inlined):
- Related spec: CON-4321 (suppressions prototype)
- Slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C01ABCD/p1634123456
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/987
- Figma: https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/signal-throttle-prototypes

Unresolved questions we should answer in grooming:
- Should suppression profiles be part of an SLA (e.g., enterprise wants strict signal retention)?
- How to measure harm from suppressed signals (false negatives) without creating too much instrumentation cost?

If we want a short-term ship: keep UI minimal — presets + 1 preview + digest to Slack. Do not include ML auto-adjust until we have strong telemetry.

-- end --
